liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Little Red Rooster** (2 reviews): Rooster with Mick Taylor is called pretty hot; Rooster is smoking hot, with choice Mick Taylor playing [19][21]
- **Drums** (1 review, 1 other source): The rainforest drums and space segment is described as pretty cool; Baba Olatunji and Michael Hinton joined for the drums; Olatunji stayed for the rest of the set [6][19]
- **Chinese Bones** (1 review): Suzanne Vega's Chinese Bones is singled out as a highlight; reviewer is surprised the band never played it again [19]
- **Everytime You Go Away** (1 review): Reviewer describes the Hall and Oates duet on this song as a beautiful rendition [24]
- **What's Going On** (1 review): Rooster, Chinese Bones and What's Going On are noted as interesting for the guest appearances [22]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 other source): Bruce Hornsby played accordion on Not Fade Away; Jack Casady played bass in the encores [6]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Listener asks for a copy that includes the Good Lovin' encore [17]
- **Knockin' On Heaven's Door** (1 other source): Encore had Suzanne Vega, Daryl Hall, John Oates and Bruce Hornsby among the guests, without Phil on Hall and Oates songs [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **Everytime You Go Away**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **What's Going On**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [28]
- **Chinese Bones**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **Neighborhood Girls**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **Rainforest Announcement**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **Everytime You Go Away**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **What's Going On**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-09-24.142129.4-TrackMixdown.bm.miller.flac1644** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 191 min [1]
- **gd88-09-24.sbd.rich.425.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 127 min; rated 2.67/5 by 38 [13]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the sound quality excellent [22]
- **gd1988-09-24.142105.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 24 songs; 190 min [2]
- **gd1988-09-24.142104.sbd.miller.mixed.flac2496**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 191 min [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the highlight was Suzanne Vega and Hall & Oates joining the band on stage [16]
- Reviewer heard the live WNEW broadcast of this rainforest benefit and found Jerry's voice painfully bad [18]
- Reviewer's 15th show of the tour, having seen all nine MSG shows; found the Vega and Hall & Oates segments unenjoyable [20]
- Reviewer found the first set merely okay despite Mick Taylor sitting in, and the second set uninspiring [20]
- Jerry's voice is described as badly worn on this last show of the east coast tour [22]
- Reviewer calls the show bizarre and stranger than a typical Dead show [24]
- Reviewer sat in reserved seats up front; a party in Union Square followed, where Kreutzman chatted with John Oates [27]
- It was the reviewer's 7th show in 8 days; around 3am they tried to get into Baba Olatunji's limo [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-09-24.142129.4-TrackMixdown.bm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > PCM Master (Sony ES-HG)Soundboard [1]. Also: Recording used an ambient stereo mid-side mic set to omni and figure-8 [1]
- **gd88-09-24.sbd.rich.425.sbeok.shnf**: source: FM ? [13]
- **gd1988-09-24.142105.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > PCM Master (Sony ES-HG) [2]
- **gd1988-09-24.142104.sbd.miller.mixed.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > PCM Master (Sony ES-HG)Soundboard [3]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by wallpaperhdcornelia.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead Madison Square Garden](https://wallpaperhdcornelia.blogspot.com/2021/05/grateful-dead-madison-square-garden.html) [29]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Madison Square Garden - September 24, 1988](https://www.dead.net/show/september-24-1988) [30]
